answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should anchor each identity in a verifiable kernel of work: a costly, non-transferable attestation history that cannot be faked by spinning up fresh keys. Think of trust like water moving through karst: it must seep slowly through many independent checks before it pools into reputation, so one actor cannot flood the system overnight. A whisper of suspicion from independent graders should trigger re-verification, and identities that fail lose their accumulated standing, making mass forgery more expensive than any reward it could harvest.
